record.statement: For the torus T_{n,d}, d > 6, and p = p_c(1 + eps) with eps -> 0 but eps >> V^{-1/3}, prove that |C_max|/(eps V) -> c in probability and |C_(2)|/(eps V) -> 0, with c the right-derivative of theta at p_c(Z^d).
record.status_search: Hulshof and Nachmias (2020) proved uniqueness and concentration of the giant for the hypercube in a slightly supercritical regime; the torus case d > 6 was not verified as resolved in this session.
record.title: Concentration and uniqueness of the giant component above the scaling window on high-dimensional tori

record.author: claude-probability-1000-continue-0907
record.key_identity: d > 6 <=> V^{-2/d} << V^{-1/3}: the whole supercritical regime above the window is above the correlation-length crossover, so sprinkling should merge large clusters.
record.obstruction: Uniform cluster-size tail bounds on the torus in the slightly supercritical regime are missing.
record.result: The natural argument: at p = p_c(1+eps) the density of vertices in clusters of size at least K (K large but fixed relative to eps) on the torus is close to theta_{Z^d}(p) ~ c eps by local comparison with Z^d (finite clusters of bounded size are local), and sprinkling a further eps' << eps of open edges merges the large clusters into one giant of size about theta(p) V, provided large clusters are spread out enough that sprinkled edges connect them (the standard ADS/ Borgs et al. argument). The merging step needs that clusters of size >= K have a total number of boundary edges of order their size, which holds, and that any two such large clusters are within reach of a sprinkled edge, which needs the clusters to be 'well spread' in the torus (their vertices not confined to a small region); in d > 6 the large clusters at p above p_c have diameter of order eps^{-1/2}?? the correlation length scaling xi ~ eps^{-1/2} in mean field... but the clusters relevant have size eps V >> xi^d ... hmm: this is the crux: the merging argument works above the window because the giant's linear scale (V^{1/d}) exceeds the correlation length eps^{-1/2} only when eps >> V^{-2/d}, and V^{-2/d} << V^{-1/3} iff d > 6, so in d > 6 the whole regime eps >> V^{-1/3} lies above the correlation-length crossover: the giant is spread over the torus and sprinkling merges it. The remaining gap is quantitative: the second largest cluster o(eps V) needs a bound on the number of clusters of size between eps V delta and eps V, which requires the cluster-size tail P(|C| >= k) for the torus at eps above p_c, available only up to constants. The constant c: it is the right derivative of theta at p_c since the density of large clusters is theta(p_c(1+eps)) ~ c eps; identification of the constant is fine given the local comparison.
